data.title: Winbond to expand Kaohsiung fab
data.description:
CATCHING UP: The market consensus of 20 percent growth in global DRAM capacity by 2028 would not meet AI demand, given AI’s rapid development, Winbond said

Winbond Electronics Corp (華邦電) yesterday said it plans to start expanding its Kaohsiung fab next year to boost DRAM capacity as the artificial intelligence (AI) boom drives a memorychip supercycle.

Construction is scheduled to start in January, with pilot production set for the end of 2029, the company said.

The Module B fab would have an initial installed capacity of 10,000 12-inch wafers per month, with total capacity of 50,000 wafers per month, Winbond said.

The company plans to use extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography to further scale up DRAM production in the later phases of the expansion, it said.

The company did not disclose the expansion’s total capital expenditure or how it would be financed.

“We have a bullish view of the [upcycle]. There is the possibility that it will last longer as long as [our new fab] enters volume production from 2030,” Winbond president James Chen (陳沛銘) said on the sidelines of an earnings conference in Taipei. “I never thought we would need EUV equipment. Now we want to buy” a machine.

The company does not think the market consensus forecast that lobal DRAM capacity would grow 20 percent by 2028 would be enough to meet AI demand, given that AI development has largely outpaced industry expectations, he said.

“The DRAM supply should continue to be very tight,” Chen said, after the shortage has last for two-and-a-half years.

To mitigate supply constraints, Winbond plans to expand its Module A capacity to about 24,000 12-inch wafers per month by the end of this year, from the current 15,000 wafers per month.

The company expects supply constraints to extend to NOR and NAND flash memory chips, which are mostly produced at the company’s Taichung fab.

As customer demand continues to surge, Winbond expects memory prices to rise further this quarter, after soaring 100 percent quarter-on-quarter last quarter. That would further boost the gross margin of its memory business above last quarter’s 70.3 percent.

The company reported a consolidated gross margin of 66.2 percent last quarter, diluted by its logic-chip business of subsidiary Nuvoton Technology Corp (新唐).

Net profit last quarter soared 140.4 percent to NT$24.32 billion (US$753.9 million) from NT$10.11 billion in the first quarter, with the increase attributable to memory price hikes and strong demand for AI applications. That reversed a loss of NT$1.31 billion in the second quarter last year.

Earnings per share rose to NT$5.4 from NT$2.25 in the first quarter. It reported a loss per share of NT$0.29 a year earlier.

Revenue expanded 56.4 percent quarter-on-quarter, and 184.7 percent year-on-year, to NT$59.84 billion last quarter.

data.title: Strong demand keeps Winmate on growth path
data.description:
AUTOMATION: Demand for high-performance industrial computers is being driven by demand for warehousing and logistics, particularly in the US, the company said

Industrial PC maker Winmate Inc (融程電訊) yesterday said it expected strong business momentum to persist in the second half of this year, driven by robust demand for mission-critical, automotive inspection, warehousing and logistics applications, after second-quarter revenue rose 42 percent and first-half revenue increased 30 percent year-on-year.

The company reported revenue of NT$1.18 billion (US$36.58 million) in the second quarter, with warehousing products accounting for 23 percent, followed by automotive inspection and electric vehicle products at 21 percent and medical products at 12 percent.

Other product categories, including ground control stations, mission-critical, factory-automation products, and marine and aviation systems, accounted for the remainder, company data showed.

Demand from the warehousing and logistics sector is expected to remain strong this quarter, particularly in the US, where rising adoption of warehouse automation is driving demand for high-performance industrial computers and edge artificial intelligence (AI) devices, Winmate chairman Ken Lu (呂谷清) said at an earnings conference in Taipei.

Orders for mission-critical applications are also projected to increase further this quarter, while automotive inspection shipments are to rebound from previously lower levels, he said.

Winmate sees meaningful shipments of medical products from next quarter through the first quarter of next year, and expects steady shipments of products for uncrewed vehicles, marine systems and military vehicles next quarter, Lu said.

In the long term, the company is looking at semiconductor equipment and industrial automation as potential growth drivers, as it targets industrial computers, rugged tablets and panel PCs for semiconductor makers, and aims to serve major German customers in industrial automation, he said.

Europe accounted for 36.1 percent of Winmate’s revenue in the second quarter, followed by North America at 34.6 percent, Asia at 25 percent, Taiwan at 3.8 percent and other markets at 0.5 percent, the company said.

Demand for edge AI is also beginning to pick up, particularly in the US warehousing and logistics market, Winmate CEO Allan Lin (林筠卿) said.

Edge AI-related products are expected to account for about 15 percent of the company’s revenue this year, he said.

Net profit last quarter rose 38 percent quarter-on-quarter and 111 percent year-on-year to NT$200 million, Winmate said.

Earnings per share rose to NT$2.48 from NT$1.8 in the previous quarter and NT$1.19 a year earlier.

Gross margin rose to 40.2 percent from 36.5 percent in the previous quarter, as the company passed higher component costs on to customers, and it is expected to remain at about 40 percent this year, Lu said.

Winmate has purchased a sufficient number of central processing units and secured long-term supply agreements with major memory suppliers, he said.

data.title: Inflation remains above 2 percent for third month
data.description:
Taiwan’s consumer inflation remained above the central bank’s 2 percent alert level for a third consecutive month last month due to higher fuel costs, airfares and food prices, the Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics (DGBAS) said yesterday.

The consumer price index (CPI) rose 2.54 percent last month from a year earlier, slowing from June’s 2.59 percent increase, while core CPI, which strips out volatile components such as fresh food and energy, rose 2.38 percent, the agency said.

“Domestic price pressures remain moderate, and there is no evidence of broad-based imported inflation despite CPI staying above 2 percent for three consecutive months,” DGBAS price statistics department head Tsai Hsiu-hui (蔡秀慧) said.

Tsai attributed last month’s increase mainly to higher fuel costs, international airfare and travel-related expenses.

Inflation could ease further this month if weather conditions do not disrupt agricultural supplies, although the figure might remain above the 2 percent threshold, she said.

Among major CPI categories, miscellaneous goods and services posted the sharpest increase, rising 3.27 percent year-on-year, as elevated gold prices pushed jewelry costs up, DGBAS data showed.

Recreation and education expenses increased 3.22 percent, driven by an 8.23 percent surge in computer equipment and software prices, as well as higher costs for overseas travel.

The producer price index (PPI) jumped 16.94 percent year-on-year, the largest increase on record and the steepest gain in about five-and-a-half years, the DGBAS said.

Import prices climbed 16.64 percent year on year, partly reflecting the impact of a weaker New Taiwan dollar that made imported goods more expensive, the agency said.

The increase was led by higher mineral product prices and a surge in the cost of electronic components and memory chips, as booming artificial intelligence demand lifted prices across the technology supply chain, it said.

As most imported products are intended for export purposes, their impact on domestic prices is limited, Tsai said.

While higher costs might affect some consumer products, such as computers and peripherals, their influence is smaller than frequently purchased items including vegetables, fruits and dining-out expenses, which carry greater weight in the CPI basket, she said.

During the first seven months of the year, CPI rose 1.8 percent from a year earlier, while PPI increased 7.93 percent.

Fuel prices remain the biggest uncertainty for Taiwan’s inflation outlook, as fluctuations in global oil prices and a relatively low comparison base from a year earlier could keep fuel-related inflation elevated in the coming months, Tsai said.

data.title: UAE fund weighs a US$6.3 billion AI data center investment in Japan
data.description:
The United Arab Emirates (UAE) is considering investing as much as ￥1 trillion (US$6.33 billion) to build an artificial intelligence (AI) data center in Japan, a person familiar with the matter said.

Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund Mubadala Investment Co would lead the investment into a 500-megawatt project in Akita Prefecture in northern Japan, which might include other foreign and domestic investors, the person said, asking not to be identified because the information is not public.

Once completed, it could become the largest data center in Japan.

The talks with the Gulf state underscore growing global interest in securing critical AI assets in countries viewed as relatively insulated from geopolitical tensions.

A spokesperson for Mubadala declined to comment.

Total investment surrounding the project, including by suppliers and other companies looking to establish operations nearby, could reach as much as ￥2 trillion, the person said.

A consortium of Japanese companies would likely handle construction and related infrastructure, they added.

As US-China tensions escalate and wars in Europe and the Middle East reshape supply chains, Japan is increasingly viewed by global investors as a stable market with relatively low geopolitical risks.

To attract funding in strategic industries, the Japanese government is in the process of designating several regions, including Akita, across the country as priority investment zones for sectors such as AI data centers and semiconductor manufacturing. It has also allocated massive financial support for related ventures.

Tokyo’s policy has rendered some substantial results. Major chip firms including Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (台積電), Tower Semiconductor Ltd and Micron Technology Inc have invested billions of dollars in the country.

Meanwhile, the oil-rich UAE has emerged as one the leading global investors in AI and its underlying infrastructure.

State-backed investor MGX, a joint venture between Mubadala and G42, has been a key vehicle through which Abu Dhabi bets on AI.

MGX last month completed its acquisition of Aligned Data Centers, which has an enterprise value of US$40 billion, alongside BlackRock Inc’s Global Infrastructure Platform and the Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Partnership.

data.title: TECO signs power deal in green energy trading push
data.description:
Teco Electric & Machinery Co (東元電機) has signed a corporate power purchase agreement with what it described as a leading semiconductor company in Taiwan, as the electromechanical equipment maker expands into the renewable energy trading market.

The long-term agreement is expected to cover more than 30 megawatts of renewable generation capacity and more than 300 million kilowatt-hours of renewable energy, Teco Electric said in a statement yesterday.

The company expects power delivery under the agreement to start by the end of this year, with supply ramping up progressively, it said.

The project is expected to generate stable, recurring revenue and predictable cash flow from electricity sales in the medium to long term, it added.

Teco Electric did not name the customer, nor disclose the financial terms of the deal.

It said only that the customer plays a key role in the global semiconductor supply chain and upholds rigorous standards for renewable energy adoption and energy management transparency.

Teco Electric expects the project to also serve as a benchmark for other companies pursuing corporate decarbonization and renewable energy procurement, it said.

Teco Electric is in discussions with several semiconductor manufacturers and high-tech companies over additional renewable energy procurement agreements, it added.

With growing customer demand, renewable energy sales could become a new growth driver for the company, it said.

As artificial intelligence applications and high-performance computing expand, high-tech companies’ electricity demand continues to rise, along with demand for reliable, long-term and large-scale renewable energy supply.

Under the corporate power purchase agreement, Teco Electric would aggregate renewable electricity from multiple power generation sites and deliver it through a diversified supply portfolio, the company said.

The approach would enhance supply reliability and dispatch flexibility while meeting the customer’s need for diversified energy sources, it said.

Teco Electric’s businesses cover electromechanical systems, electric power, air-conditioning equipment, and energy and system automation.

First-half revenue rose 5.92 percent year-on-year to NT$30.79 billion (US$954.4 million), a five-year high for the period, driven by demand from data centers, offshore wind power projects and engineering projects for power generators, it said.

The company has been transforming itself from an equipment manufacturer into an integrated energy services provider, with the aim of supplying end-to-end services from engineering and construction to asset management, renewable energy procurement, energy optimization and power dispatch, it said.

data.title: GlobalWafers forecasts growth
data.description:
SECURING SUPPLY: Customers are seeking longer-term contracts, while the company discusses potential price hikes amid rising energy, logistics and labor costs, it said

GlobalWafers Co (環球晶圓) on Tuesday said it expects revenue to grow at a “meaningful” rate next year, rather than in the second half of this year as previously anticipated, after a blaze at its fab in Novara, Italy, slowed its sales momentum.

While the incident should have minimal impact on the company’s 8-inch wafer manufacturing equipment, production would take time to recover, the world’s third-largest silicon wafer supplier said.

“Our revenue [this year] should be flat or slightly higher than last year ... because of the fire. Otherwise, we are supposed to have much higher revenue,” GlobalWafers chairperson Doris Hsu (徐秀蘭) told investors.

The company expects meaningful revenue growth next year, driven by increasing demand for advanced 12-inch wafers and 12-inch silicon-on-insulator wafers used in silicon photonics, she said, adding that additional 12-inch wafer capacity would come online to meet demand.

The industry’s supply-demand conditions have gradually improved and order visibility has lengthened, Hsu said.

The outlook for the second half of this year is “meaningfully stronger” than in the first half, with robust demand for wafers used in high-bandwidth memory chips for artificial intelligence servers, as well as in industrial, power-management and energy-related applications, GlobalWafers said.

The uptrend has boosted the company’s factory utilization rates across its 12, 8 and 6-inch wafer production lines, it added.

Given rising demand and tightening supply, an increasing number of customers are seeking new long-term supply agreements with longer terms than in previous years, it said.

As rising energy, logistics, raw material and labor costs, along with more demanding wafer specifications and technology requirements, drive up overall costs, the company is discussing price hikes with customers, it said.

The company expects wafer prices on the spot market to rise in the second half of this year and remain elevated through the first quarter next year, Hsu said.

GlobalWafers on Tuesday reported net profit of NT$3.78 billion (US$116.97 million) in the second quarter, more than double the NT$1.68 billion a year earlier, and 99 percent higher than the previous quarter’s NT$1.9 billion.

Earnings per share rose to NT$7.9 from NT$3.52 a year earlier and NT$3.97 a quarter earlier.

Gross margin dropped to 20.6 percent, compared with 25.8 percent in the second quarter last year and 20.8 percent in the first quarter.

data.title: Forex reserves fall for second month
data.description:
Taiwan’s foreign-exchange reserves fell for a second consecutive month last month as overseas investors repatriated stock gains and dividend income, boosting US dollar demand and prompting the central bank to step in to smooth currency-market volatility.

The reserves fell by US$2.88 billion to US$594.27 billion from US$597.15 billion a month earlier, as foreign investors repatriated stock-market gains and dividends from Taiwan-listed companies, central bank Department of Foreign Exchange Director-General Eugene Tsai (蔡炯民) said yesterday.

Against the backdrop, the New Taiwan dollar weakened 1.66 percent against the US dollar, even as most major currencies gained against the greenback. The US dollar index shed 1.26 percent during the month.

Foreign selling pressure in Taiwan’s equity market has subsided since the end of last month, with foreign investors turning net buyers yesterday, Tsai said.

While some dividend payments remain in Taiwan for reinvestment, most funds have historically been transferred abroad, he said.

The impact of dividend outflows on the local currency tend to be temporary, depending on market conditions and whether stock valuations attract foreign capital back into Taiwan, he said.

For example, in July 2024, the NT dollar weakened amid dividend remittances before rebounding in August that year as funds returned to the market, Tsai said.

A similar pattern occurred in the first quarter of last year, when foreign outflows temporarily pressured the local currency before they resumed following broader US dollar movements.

Tsai also rejected comparisons with South Korea, where the won strengthened last month despite foreign investors selling shares, as the NT dollar faced heavier dividend-related outflows, while foreign investors in South Korea might have rotated funds from equities into bonds, rather than exiting the market altogether, he said.

Taiwan’s foreign investors are primarily focused on equities and hold only limited positions in the domestic bond market, he added.

data.title: Nanya Technology raises expenditures in chip ramp-up
data.description:
Nanya Technology Corp (南亞科技) yesterday raised its capital expenditure budget for this year by about 34 percent to a ceiling of NT$69.7 billion (US$2.16 billion), from NT$52 billion set earlier, as the DRAM chipmaker invests in new manufacturing equipment to accelerate the production ramp-up of next-generation chips.

The additional funds would be used to make advance payments on equipment needed to expand its new 12-inch fab, Fab 5A, Nanya Technology said in a statement.

Its board of directors also approved up to NT$346.6 billion in capital expenditures for Fab 5A from this year through 2029, including purchases of extreme ultraviolet equipment, to support the first-phase capacity expansion of 35,900 wafer starts per month, it said.

Nanya Technology plans to produce DRAM chips at the fab using 10 nanometer-class technology and ramp up the fab’s monthly capacity to 30,000 wafer starts per month in 2028 and 35,900 in 2029.

The fab’s planned full capacity is 45,000 wafer starts per month, it said.

The board also approved a US$2.1 billion capital injection into Nanya Technology International Ltd (南亞科技國際), a wholly owned subsidiary, to reduce the impact of foreign exchange rate fluctuations on operations.

The board also approved the transfer of 715,000 common shares of PieceMakers Technology Inc (補丁科技) to the underwriter for no less than NT$545 a share in connection with PieceMakers’ Emerging Stock Board listing.

Following the transfer, Nanya Technology’s stake in PieceMakers would fall to 33.96 percent, it said.

It would book a disposal gain of NT$360 million, it added.

data.title: Advantech sees solid sales growth
data.description:
GLOBAL TRENDS: Advantech expects revenue from North America, China and Europe to grow this quarter, driven by the medical equipment and AI infrastructure industries

Industrial PC maker Advantech Co (研華) yesterday said it expects to post double-digit percentage revenue growth this quarter, driven by robust demand for semiconductor equipment, artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and edge AI products.

Order momentum is expected to remain strong in the second half of this year, with the book-to-bill ratio rising to 1.64 last month from 1.44 in the second quarter and monthly orders reaching a record US$574 million, Advantech president Eric Chen (陳清熙) told an earnings conference in Taipei.

The company secured 123 design wins in the first half of this year, which are expected to generate US$444 million in revenue and provide growth momentum, he said.

Advantech’s revenue rose 46 percent year-on-year to NT$26.13 billion (US$808.6 million) in the second quarter and grew 32.18 percent to NT$46.51 billion in the first half of this year.

North America accounted for 29 percent of the company’s revenue in the first half, followed by China at 24 percent and Europe at 16 percent, Chen said.

The company expects revenue from North America, China and Europe to each grow by a double-digit percentage this quarter, driven mainly by medical equipment, AI infrastructure and semiconductor-related industries, he said.

Advantech reported that net profit last quarter rose 36 percent quarter-on-quarter and 127 percent year-on-year to NT$4.52 billion.

Earnings per share rose to NT$5.2 from NT$3.85 the previous quarter and NT$2.3 a year earlier.

Gross margin fell to 37.7 percent last quarter from 39.1 percent in the previous quarter due to higher component costs and is expected to remain at about 37.7 percent this quarter, Chen said.

Advantech has passed some of the higher costs on to customers, with further hikes possible after suppliers, including Nvidia Corp and Intel Corp, announced plans to raise prices, he said.

The company expects sufficient component supply this quarter and is working to secure supply for the fourth quarter, Advantech Intelligent Systems Sector president Linda Tsai (蔡淑妍) said.

Edge AI applications are expected to remain a key growth driver in the second half, led by strong demand for semiconductor equipment and AI data centers, Advantech embedded Internet of Things president Miller Chang (張家豪) said.

Physical AI applications, including AI factories and robotics, are also growing rapidly, prompting Advantech to continue increasing investment in these areas, Chang said.

AI-related products saw sales increase 250 percent year-on-year, accounted for 22.5 percent of total revenue in the first half of this year and are on track to reach 30 percent for the full year, he said.

The company has about 150 robotics-related projects in its pipeline, covering autonomous mobile robots, cobots and humanoid robots, he said.
